facebook.content_angle: Hand entry and catch position — how a poor hand entry angle creates immediate drag and kills the power of every stroke before it even begins, with a simple fingertip drill to fix it
facebook.post_text:
Fix this one thing and every stroke gets faster. 🎯

Most club swimmers drop their hand into the water at the wrong angle — thumb-first or flat-palmed — and bleed power before the catch even starts.

You can be fit, strong, and still slow because of this.

👉 A thumb-first entry creates an air pocket that disrupts your catch and adds drag with every single stroke
👉 Research shows correcting hand entry angle alone can reduce stroke count per length by 2–3 strokes
👉 Fewer strokes at the same pace = less energy burned = faster splits when it counts

Elite swimmers aren't just fitter than you. They waste less. ⚡

✔️ Enter fingertips first, hand angled slightly outward (10–15 degrees)
✔️ Extend fully before the catch — don't rush the pull
✔️ Drill it: fingertip drag drill, 4 x 50m focused, every session this week
